annotation.emotional_arc: From existential questioning and fear to resilience and courage

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The earth is depicted as an active, vocal entity calling out to humanity, emphasizing our deep connection to nature and the soil.
acceptable_visual_variants: A wide shot of rich brown soil with green sprouts under a vast sky, with soft golden light suggesting a calling presence.
A person kneeling and touching the earth, sensing its silent message through the soil.
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: The earth speaks by calling out
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing a literal human face or mouth emerging from the soil of the globe to speak, which looks cartoonish or monstrous.
metaphor_spans.tenor: The natural world or earth as an active presence communicating with humans
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a vast, beautiful landscape of soil and earth with subtle wind currents or light patterns suggesting a voice or presence, without drawing literal human facial features on the ground.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation adds 'to return to it too' to complete the rhyme, which is not explicitly present in the original Hindi text 'माटी में क्यों डरता है' (why do you fear in the soil/dust).

The intimate, direct address of the pronoun 'तू' (tu) and the colloquial, spiritually-toned term 'बंदे' (bande - O human/servant of God) are flattened into the more generic 'O being, what do you do?'.

stanzas.loss_note: The translation adds the metaphor 'Wrapped in fear's shroud' which is not present in the original Hindi text; the original simply asks why one wastes this precious journey.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Nature (trees, plants, flowers) is personified as laughing and speaking to remind humans to enjoy the journey of life.
acceptable_visual_variants: A close-up of dew-covered flower buds opening in morning sunlight, conveying a natural 'smile'.
A sunny garden scene with trees swaying in a light wind, suggesting cheerful movement.
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: These trees, plants, flowers, and buds all speak while laughing repeatedly
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Drawing literal cartoon faces with wide open laughing mouths on tree trunks and flower petals.
metaphor_spans.source_span_original:
यह पेड़-पौधे, फूल-कलियाँ,
सब कहते हैं हँस-हँस के
metaphor_spans.source_span_translation:
These trees, plants, and blooms,
All laugh and say aloud
metaphor_spans.source_term: यह पेड़-पौधे, फूल-कलियाँ, सब कहते हैं हँस-हँस के
metaphor_spans.tenor: The vibrant, joyful, and lively appearance of blooming nature
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict lush, vibrant green trees and colorful flowers swaying gently in the breeze under bright sunlight, capturing a natural sense of joy and movement.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Life is conceptualized as a precious journey or travel route to be experienced rather than wasted.
acceptable_visual_variants: A path winding through a forest with alternating patches of sunlight and shadow.
A lone traveler walking along a scenic ridge at dawn.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting a literal traveler with suitcases or a passport, which misses the existential nature of life's journey.
metaphor_spans.source_span_original: जीवन के इस अनमोल सफर को
metaphor_spans.source_term: जीवन के इस अनमोल सफर को
metaphor_spans.tenor: The course of human life over time
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Show a winding path leading through a beautiful, changing landscape towards a bright horizon, symbolizing the passage of time and experiences.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation introduces the metaphor 'Wrapped in fear’s shroud' to create a rhyme with 'aloud', which has no textual basis in the original Hindi line 'तू क्यों व्यर्थ गंवाता है' (why do you waste it in vain).
The reduplicative, rhythmic quality of 'हँस-हँस के' (laughing repeatedly/joyfully) is simplified to 'say aloud'.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The earth is personified again as calling out to guide the human traveler.
acceptable_visual_variants: A wide shot of rich brown soil with green sprouts under a vast sky, with soft golden light suggesting a calling presence.
A person kneeling and touching the earth, sensing its silent message through the soil.
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: The earth speaks by calling out
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing a literal human face or mouth emerging from the soil of the globe to speak, which looks cartoonish or monstrous.
metaphor_spans.tenor: The natural world or earth as an active presence communicating with humans
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a vast, beautiful landscape of soil and earth with subtle wind currents or light patterns suggesting a voice or presence, without drawing literal human facial features on the ground.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Joy and sorrow are conceptualized as shadows or alternating patches of light and shade that one walks through.
acceptable_visual_variants: A traveler walking on a path that goes through both bright sunny clearings and shaded forest canopy.
A landscape at dusk where long shadows stretch across sunlit fields.
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: In this shadow of happiness and sadness
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Drawing literal dark silhouettes or monsters labeled 'sadness' chasing a person.
metaphor_spans.source_span_translation: In the shadows of joy and sorrow
metaphor_spans.tenor: The alternating, transient phases of happiness and sadness in life
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a path with dappled light, where bright sunny patches alternate with cool, dark shadows cast by overhead trees.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Courage is conceptualized as an ornament or something beautiful to be adorned, cultivated, or displayed.
acceptable_visual_variants: A person adjusting their posture to stand strong against a gust of wind, with a determined expression.
A glowing lantern held high by a traveler, illuminating the path ahead in the shadows.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing a person literally hanging decorations or ornaments on a abstract concept or a glowing heart, which looks confusing.
metaphor_spans.tenor: Cultivating, strengthening, and displaying inner bravery
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a person standing tall and resolute on a path, with a warm, steady inner light radiating from their chest, symbolizing adorned courage.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation renders 'साहस को तू सजाता जा' (keep adorning/decorating courage) as 'Let courage light your day', changing the active, creative metaphor of 'decorating' or 'beautifying' one's life with courage into a more passive illumination metaphor.

annotation.theme: The earth and nature urge humanity to overcome the fear of mortality and march forward with courage through life's joys and sorrows.

original_poem:
धरती कहे पुकार के,  
बंदे तू क्या करता है,  
माटी से तू पैदा हुआ,  
माटी में क्यों डरता है।  

यह पेड़-पौधे, फूल-कलियाँ,  
सब कहते हैं हँस-हँस के,  
जीवन के इस अनमोल सफर को,  
तू क्यों व्यर्थ गंवाता है।  

धरती कहे पुकार के,  
अपने पथ पर बढ़ता जा,  
सुख-दुख की इस छाया में,  
साहस को तू सजाता जा।
translated_poem:
The earth calls out,  
“O being, what do you do?  
Born from this soil,  
Why do you fear to return to it too?”

These trees, plants, and blooms,  
All laugh and say aloud,  
Why waste this precious journey of life,  
Wrapped in fear’s shroud?

The earth calls out,  
March forward on your way,  
In the shadows of joy and sorrow,  
Let courage light your day.
